text_md: Note that d-distinction implies ‘future or past d-distinction’ which implies weak d-distinction. This result is a bit surprising since the function d contains much more information than the chronological relation. Note that we do not assume that d is finite or continuous. For the converse, suppose that dq ≤ dp, then if r ∈ I+(q) we have dq(r) > 0 so dp(r) > 0 which implies r ∈ I+(p). By the arbitrariness of r, I+(q) ⊂ - I+(p). We recall [43, Def. 4.46] that a spacetime is future distinguishing if I+(p) = - I+(q) ⇒ p = q (and similarly in the past case). A spacetime is weakly distinguishing if I+(p) = I+(q) and I−(p) = I−(q) ⇒ p = q, cf. [43, Def. 4.47]. A spacetime is distinguishing if I+(p) = I+(q) or I−(p) = I−(q) ⇒ p = q, cf. [43, Def. 4.59].
